<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard, clean Rust PKGBUILD for `bluet`, a Bluetooth device manager. The `source` array fetches the tagged GitHub release archive (`$url/archive/v$pkgver.tar.gz`) and it is pinned with a real `sha256sums` entry (not SKIP), so the tarball is integrity-verified.

The lifecycle functions are all conventional: `prepare()` runs `cargo fetch --locked`, `build()` runs `cargo build --release --locked` (locked dependency resolution, good practice), `check()` runs the test suite plus `desktop-file-validate`, and `package()` installs the compiled binary, a `.desktop` file, an icon, README, and license files into `$pkgdir` using `install`. There are no network calls to unexpected hosts, no `curl`/`wget`/`eval`, no obfuscated or encoded strings, no credential/data access, and no writes outside the package's own installation scope.

The GitHub URL matches the declared maintainer's repository, and the entire workflow is consistent with ordinary AUR Rust packaging.
</details>
